meta.title: Uninstall ProxMenux | ProxMenux Documentation
meta.description: Clean ProxMenux uninstaller with optional removal of jq and dialog, cleanup of legacy translation files and the Monitor service, and restoration of system-file backups.
meta.ogDescription: Cleanly remove ProxMenux from a Proxmox host with optional dependency cleanup.

header.title: Uninstall ProxMenux
header.description: Removes ProxMenux from the Proxmox host with an interactive flow: confirmation, optional dependency removal, ProxMenux Monitor service cleanup, restoration of /root/.bashrc and /etc/motd backups. Shows a progress bar throughout.

scopeWarn.title: Affects the ProxMenux install only — not your VMs / CTs / storage
scopeWarn.body: Uninstalling ProxMenux removes the ProxMenux scripts, the menu launcher, the optional Monitor service and any backups ProxMenux took of system files when you installed it. It does not touch your VMs, containers, storage, network configuration, Fail2Ban, NVIDIA driver or anything else you installed via ProxMenux. Those stay as they are.

flow.heading: The uninstall flow
items: Confirmation dialog. Yes/no — “Are you sure you want to uninstall ProxMenux?”
Dependency removal checklist. Offers jq and dialog. Both boxes are OFF by default; select only dependencies that no other application needs.

Removal runs with a progress bar. Removes any leftover legacy translation environment, the menu launcher, the /usr/local/share/proxmenux/ tree, the ProxMenux Monitor service if present together with the notification target it registered in Proxmox VE (proxmenux-webhook and its matcher), the dependencies you ticked, and finally restores the system file backups (see below).
Completion dialog. Lists removed dependencies and exits.

deps.heading: Dependency removal: what's offered
deps.intro: The checklist offers jq and dialog. Neither box is checked by default: other applications may use these system-wide packages, so keeping them is safer.
deps.warnBody: The current checklist offers jq and dialog, not python3. These are system packages that other tools may need. Removal can also remove dependent packages or unused dependencies. Keep required packages and review any proposed removal before running apt manually.

removed.heading: What gets removed
removed.code:
/usr/local/bin/menu                                  # the launcher
/usr/local/share/proxmenux/                          # everything: scripts, config, cache, version
/opt/googletrans-env/                                # leftover legacy translation environment
/etc/systemd/system/proxmenux-monitor.service        # Monitor service unit
/root/.config/proxmenux-monitor/                     # Monitor config dir
                                                     # + dependencies you ticked in the checklist

restored.heading: What gets restored
items: If /root/.bashrc.bak exists → renamed back to /root/.bashrc (your original bashrc returns).
If /etc/motd.bak exists → renamed back to /etc/motd. Otherwise the ProxMenux line (“This system is optimised by: ProxMenux”) is stripped from the existing motd with sed.

othersCallout.title: Other ProxMenux-installed components stay
othersCallout.body: Anything ProxMenux installed via other menus — Fail2Ban, Lynis, NVIDIA drivers, post-install tweaks — is not touched by this uninstaller. Each has its own uninstall flow inside its respective menu (or you can remove with apt directly). Look at Show Version Information first to see what's registered.

manual.heading: Manual uninstall
manual.intro: If for some reason the menu uninstaller can't run (e.g. dialog already missing), the equivalent manual sequence:
manual.code:
# 1. Stop and remove the Monitor service (if installed)
systemctl stop proxmenux-monitor.service 2>/dev/null
systemctl disable proxmenux-monitor.service 2>/dev/null
rm -f /etc/systemd/system/proxmenux-monitor.service
rm -rf /root/.config/proxmenux-monitor
systemctl daemon-reload
systemctl reset-failed 2>/dev/null

# 2. Remove a leftover legacy translation environment
rm -rf /opt/googletrans-env

# 3. Remove ProxMenux files
rm -f /usr/local/bin/menu
rm -rf /usr/local/share/proxmenux

# 4. Restore backups
[ -f /root/.bashrc.bak ] && mv /root/.bashrc.bak /root/.bashrc
[ -f /etc/motd.bak ] && mv /etc/motd.bak /etc/motd \
    || sed -i '/This system is optimised by: ProxMenux/d' /etc/motd

reinstall.heading: Reinstalling later
reinstall.body: Run the official ProxMenux installer again. Current releases use one installation path with all eight interface languages included.

troubleshoot.heading: Troubleshooting
troubleshoot.hangTitle: Uninstall stalls while removing a legacy translation environment
troubleshoot.hangBody: Current releases remove a leftover environment with rm -rf /opt/googletrans-env; they do not run pip uninstall. If this step stalls, inspect it from another shell and check the host filesystem before retrying.
troubleshoot.aptTitle: apt warns about packages still in use during dependency removal
troubleshoot.aptBody: Selected packages are marked automatic and passed to apt-get -y --purge autoremove. This does not guarantee that dependent services are protected. Leave dependencies unchecked if other tools need them; review apt’s proposed removals before any manual cleanup.
troubleshoot.motdTitle: MOTD still shows the ProxMenux line after uninstall
troubleshoot.motdBody: Either no /etc/motd.bak existed and the sed strip didn't match (e.g. the line was modified). Edit /etc/motd by hand and remove any leftover ProxMenux line.
